newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil again discounts imminent brake on economy.
newsitem.headline: Brazil again discounts imminent brake on economy.

text.p: The Brazilian Finance Ministry's economic policy secretary Jose Roberto Mendonca de Barros said it remained unclear whether the economy was growing too fast and said there were no plans for a shift in monetary policy.
"The picture remains cloudy," Mendonca de Barros told reporters. "The government is not convinced of the necessity for any change in monetary or economic policy."
Mendonca de Barros said there were clear signs that insolvency was on the rise and that consumer sales were easing.
He said the latest figures from Sao Paulo pointed to a 2.7 percent drop in physical sales compared with January.
The number of bounced checks had hit a new record of 5.7 per every 1,000 in February, up from the last peak in June 1995, when 5.2 of every 1,000 checks were returned for insufficient funds.
"So there's no real sign of overheating," Mendonca de Barros said.
Brazil's widening trade deficit, which has swelled to $2.8 billion so far in 1997 after last year's $5.5 billion, has led to speculation the government may slam the brakes on demand.
The Finance Ministry also suggested in its monthly report on the economy it expects to continue with a policy of gradually decreasing interest rates.

It said markets expected rates to stabilize in May because by then the so-called "coupon cambial" -- the spread between fixed-income investments and currency devaluation -- would have fallen below 11.0 percent.
"But foreign capital in the Brazilian economy has tended to be longer term and, thus, less sensitive to the coupon cambial," the ministry said.
